name: Horizontal Nursing Badge Reference Cards (49 Cards)
seoTitle: Horizontal Nursing Badge Reference Cards Set
metaDescription: A set of 49 horizontal badge cards with quick references like lab values, EKG basics, and vitals, a practical gift for nursing students and new LPNs.
summary: A practical clinical and school gift: 49 horizontal reference cards that hang behind a badge, covering everyday basics like lab values, EKG, and vitals.
whyItWorks: Ask a nursing student what they wish they had on their first clinical rotation and many will say a way to check normal lab ranges without pulling out a phone in front of a patient. Badge cards solve that quietly. They clip behind an ID and flip open when needed, so the information rides along all shift without taking up a scrubs pocket.

The horizontal format matters more than it sounds. Some hospitals and schools issue badges that sit sideways, and vertical cards can hang awkwardly behind them. If you know the recipient wears a landscape style badge, a set built for that orientation is a thoughtful detail that shows you paid attention. With 49 cards, the recipient can pick the handful they actually use on their unit and keep the rest at home for studying. It works as a small standalone gift or as part of a clinicals care package with good pens and a penlight.
goodToKnow: Confirm which way the recipient's badge hangs before buying, since this set is the horizontal version.
Check the listing to see whether a badge holder or ring is included or if the cards attach to an existing reel.
Reference cards are study and convenience aids, so the recipient should still follow their facility's own protocols.

faq.q: Is this better for students or working nurses?
faq.a: It leans toward nursing students and newer LPNs who are still memorizing ranges. Experienced nurses may only use a few cards, so it is best for someone early in their career.

faq.q: What if the badge orientation is unknown?
faq.a: Ask casually or look at a photo of them in uniform. If you cannot find out, a vertical set is the more common choice.
